<issue>
set_value fails with TypeError when setting nested values

```
d = {'foo': {'bar': 1}}
set_value(d, 'foo.bar.baz', 42)
```

TypeError: 'int' object does not support item assignment

The function fails when trying to set a nested value where one of the intermediate values is not a dictionary. In the example above, 'bar' already contains an integer value, but the function tries to treat it as a dictionary to set 'baz'.

This happens because the new implementation doesn't check if the intermediate values are dictionaries before trying to access them as dictionaries.

Here's a simple reproduction:

```python
from marshmallow.utils import set_value

# This works fine
d = {}
set_value(d, 'foo.bar', 42)
print(d)  # {'foo': {'bar': 42}}

# This also works
d = {'foo': {}}
set_value(d, 'foo.bar', 42)
print(d)  # {'foo': {'bar': 42}}

# This fails
d = {'foo': 42}
set_value(d, 'foo.bar', 99)
# TypeError: 'int' object does not support item assignment
```
</issue>
